groups.title: Contentful Data Modelling
groups.question: Your marketing team wants to write blog posts in Contentful, preview drafts before publishing and use rich formatting. Explain how you would model the content and render it.

followUps.Content types, fields, and validation in: What is a content type in Contentful?
followUps.Preview versus published environments an: How do preview and delivery differ in Contentful?
followUps.Rich text field rendering in React compo: Why can't you render a rich text field as plain HTML directly?

evidence.text: A content type defines the structure of entries, like a table schema.
Each field has a type, such as text, date or reference.
Validations like required or unique keep content consistent.

notEnough: Only saying content types define content.

evidence.text: Contentful has separate APIs and keys for preview and delivery.
The preview API returns draft entries.
Editors check drafts on a preview site before they are published to production.

notEnough: Only saying you can preview content.

evidence.text: Rich text is stored as a structured tree of nodes, not HTML.
A renderer library turns that tree into React elements.
Custom renderers control how embedded entries and assets appear.

notEnough: Only saying you use a renderer.

groups.title: Contentful API Concepts
groups.question: Your site reads blog posts from Contentful, and a script needs to create hundreds of entries during a migration. Explain which Contentful APIs you would use.

followUps.Content Delivery API vs Content Manageme: When would you use the Content Delivery API and when the Content Management API?
followUps.GraphQL API for typed content queries in: What does Contentful's GraphQL API give you?

evidence.text: The Content Delivery API is read-only, CDN-backed and serves published content to the site.
The Content Management API can write content and is used for migrations and tooling.
Management tokens must never be exposed in the frontend.

notEnough: Only saying one reads and one writes.

evidence.text: It exposes your content types as typed GraphQL queries.
You request exactly the fields a component needs.
Queries can sit next to the components that use them.

groups.title: Querying and Fetching Contentful
groups.question: Your blog page fetches posts from Contentful, then makes another request for each author, and pages are slow. Explain how you would fetch entries and linked content efficiently.

followUps.Fetching entries with the Contentful JS: How would you fetch only blog posts with the fields you need?
followUps.Querying linked assets and nested refere: How do you get linked authors and images without extra requests?

evidence.text: The JavaScript SDK wraps the delivery API with methods to get entries.
You filter by content type to get only blog posts.
Selecting specific fields reduces the response size.

notEnough: Only saying you use the SDK.

evidence.text: Entries can reference other entries and assets.
The include parameter resolves linked items in the same response.
This avoids making a request per linked item.

groups.title: Assets, Media and Gatsby Integration
groups.question: Your site uses Contentful images that are too large, and you are moving the site to Gatsby. Explain how you would serve images efficiently and connect Contentful to Gatsby.

followUps.Contentful Image API for on-demand image: How can you resize Contentful images without your own image server?
followUps.gatsby-source-contentful plugin setup an: How does gatsby-source-contentful get content into a Gatsby site?

evidence.text: Contentful serves assets through a CDN.
URL parameters control width, height, format and quality.
This lets you request the right size for each screen.
The plugin pulls published entries into Gatsby's GraphQL layer at build time.
It is configured with the space id and an access token.
The token is kept in environment variables, not in the code.

notEnough: Only saying it connects Gatsby to Contentful.
